subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which part of the four-layer collaboration stack, if any, should OpenClaw core own first?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested primitives, and choosing the first slice requires product and security intent across core state storage, memory visibility, delegation, plugin seams, and cost policy.

options.title: Keep RFC and scope a core design
options.body: Use this issue to define the smallest core-owned primitive and its security/storage contract before any implementation PR.

options.title: Split a narrow follow-up
options.body: Move one bounded slice, such as a meeting primitive, blackboard API, or cost-governed spawn policy, into its own issue once the owner boundary is clear.

options.title: Route orchestration out of core
options.body: Keep optional collaboration frameworks in plugins or ClawHub until they prove a missing core API or SDK seam.

recommendation.title: Keep RFC and scope a core design
recommendation.body: Use this issue to define the smallest core-owned primitive and its security/storage contract before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing signal for subagent collaboration product direction and related maintainer scoping.
